cards.title: Splunk Detection Engineering
cards.summary: SPL queries, Risk-Based Alerting, and operational tuning for enterprise Splunk

items.text: assign risk scores per event; alert on cumulative risk threshold crossing. Dramatically reduces alert fatigue vs rule-per-event approach.
items.note: Risk objects: user, system, IP. Score threshold typically 100-200 before incident opens.

items.text: use `| tstats` over `index=` for high-volume searches. 10-100× faster on summarized data.
items.note: `| tstats count WHERE index=winevent by host _time span=1m`

items.text: normalize hostnames, IPs, users. Enables pivot-based investigation and automatic enrichment.
trigger SOAR playbooks, EDR isolation, or firewall blocks directly from an alert action. Connects detection to response.
`| eventstats` for fleet baselines; `| streamstats` for sequential/time-window analysis.
attackers living in Splunk will search your hunting activity. Audit search logs. Use role-based search head separation for IR hunts.

cards.title: Microsoft Sentinel
cards.summary: Cloud-native SIEM - KQL-based, deep M365/Azure integration, UEBA built-in

items.text: master `| where` `| summarize` `| join` `| render` before writing analytics rules.
items.note: Use `let` statements to stage subqueries for readability and reuse.

items.text: Scheduled (periodic query), NRT Near-Real-Time (streaming, <5 min latency), Fusion (ML cross-signal correlation).
import threat intel IOCs, asset inventory, or known-good baselines as lookup tables. Use `_GetWatchlist()` in rules for enrichment.
built-in baseline engine. Anomaly insights feed into Fusion rule engine for low-and-slow detection without manual baselines.
Logic Apps trigger on incident creation. Auto-enrich, auto-close FPs, auto-notify, auto-isolate via MDE action.
Data Collection Rules filter at ingestion time. Drop noisy sources (Defender endpoint verbose logs, raw NetFlow) before billing.

cards.title: Sysmon Deployment
cards.summary: Essential endpoint telemetry for Windows - process, network, memory, registry in one agent

items.text: 1 process · 3 network · 7 DLL load · 8 RemoteThread · 10 ProcessAccess (LSASS) · 11 file · 12/13 registry · 15 ADS · 17/18 pipe · 22 DNS · 25 process tamper
`GrantedAccess 0x1FFFFF` or `0x1010` = LSASS dump attempt. Exclude known AV/EDR by process hash not just name.
start with SwiftOnSecurity config; upgrade to Olaf Hartong's modular config for mature environments. Both on GitHub.
captures process→IP correlation. Enables C2 beacon detection even over standard ports (80/443).
captures DNS query + requesting process. Crucial for C2-over-DNS where HTTP logs alone miss it.
filter aggressively. Ship all Sysmon raw = expensive and noisy. Filter known-good processes per event type.

cards.title: Elastic Security
cards.summary: Open-source ELK stack with commercial security features - scalable and detection-as-code friendly

items.text: Elastic Common Schema maps all source fields to standard names. Detection rules become portable across log sources.
EQL (Event Query Language for sequence detection), ESQL (new analytical), ML anomaly, threshold, indicator match.
900+ MITRE-aligned at `github.com/elastic/detection-rules`. Always validate and tune FP rate before enabling in production.
unified collection agent replacing multiple Beats. Manages policies centrally, supports endpoint protection and network capture.
visual investigation interface. Attach findings to cases for IR documentation and evidence chain.
new query language optimized for large analytical scans. Faster than EQL for fleet-wide baseline analysis.

cards.title: Microsoft Defender for Endpoint
cards.summary: Deeply integrated Windows telemetry, ASR rules, cloud-ML, and native response

items.text: 16 rules blocking specific behaviors. Enable audit mode first; transition to block after 2-4 weeks. Critical: block Office child processes, block LSASS credential theft.
prevents local disable of Defender settings. Enforce via Intune. Without this, malware can trivially disable AV before payload drop.
`DeviceProcessEvents` · `DeviceNetworkEvents` · `DeviceRegistryEvents` · `DeviceFileEvents`. Write custom hunts in security.microsoft.com portal.
remote shell on any enrolled device. Run scripts, collect files, kill processes without VPN tunnel.
Windows 11 feature blocking unsigned/uncredentialed binaries. Complement with WDAC policies for enterprise coverage.
hypervisor-isolated LSASS prevents credential extraction even with LSASS handle access.

cards.title: CrowdStrike Falcon
cards.summary: Industry-leading behavioral EDR - kernel sensor, cloud ML, and Overwatch managed detection

items.text: enable "Extra Paranoid" protection mode for Tier 0 assets (DCs, PAWs, executive devices) where false positives are acceptable.
behavioral detection based on process lineage, command line patterns, and network behavior. Not signature-based - survives malware recompilation.
vulnerability management prioritized by active exploitation in the wild. Bridges EDR telemetry with vulnerability data for real-world risk scoring.
live remote shell. Run scripts, kill processes, network isolate from Falcon console without agent reinstall.
CrowdStrike's managed threat hunting team layered on your telemetry. Worth the cost for organizations without a 24/7 SOC.
query raw sensor telemetry with Splunk-like syntax. Pivot from any IOC across the entire fleet in minutes.

cards.title: Velociraptor
cards.summary: Open-source DFIR platform - hunt and collect at scale across thousands of endpoints simultaneously

items.text: SQL-like language for endpoint queries. Collect artifacts, parse registry hives, hunt IOC patterns fleet-wide in real time.
pre-built collection templates: Windows.KapeFiles (KAPE triage), Windows.Network.Netstat, Windows.System.Pslist, Windows.Detection.Autoruns.
push VQL to every endpoint simultaneously. Results stream back in seconds for 10,000+ endpoint fleets.
standalone collector for air-gapped or isolated hosts. Run from USB, results saved locally, import to server.
correlate collected artifacts across hosts into attack timelines automatically with built-in analysis.
completely free, self-hosted on PostgreSQL or MySQL. Cost-effective alternative for orgs without commercial EDR budget.

cards.title: SentinelOne Singularity
cards.summary: Autonomous AI-driven EDR with rollback capability - can respond without human intervention

items.text: contextual process tree linking every event (process, file, network, registry) into coherent attack narratives. Dramatically accelerates triage.
kill, quarantine, rollback without analyst approval. Configure carefully - autonomous kill decisions need policy review before enabling.
uses Windows Volume Shadow Copy to restore ransomware-encrypted files automatically. Can recover entire encrypted drives in minutes.
raw telemetry query interface. Pivot on any observable (hash, IP, cmdline, registry key) across the entire fleet.
network discovery via sensor telemetry to identify unmanaged devices. No additional scanner needed for internal asset discovery.
live remote investigation session without VPN. Scripts, file collection, process kill from SentinelOne console.

title: Detection Engineering
description: Building, testing, and maintaining detections that analysts trust. Coverage over the MITRE ATT&CK framework, rule lifecycle management, and false-positive reduction are the core disciplines.

callouts.title: Detection Quality Rule
callouts.body: A detection that fires constantly and gets ignored is worse than no detection. Alert fatigue kills SOC effectiveness. Measure false-positive rate per rule weekly and tune ruthlessly - the goal is trust, not coverage theater.

cards.title: SIGMA Rules
cards.summary: Vendor-agnostic detection rule format - write once, deploy to any SIEM via sigma-cli

items.text: YAML-based. Key fields: `logsource` (category + product), `detection` (selection + filter conditions), `level` (informational → critical).
items.note: Compile with: `sigma convert -t splunk -p splunk_windows rule.yml`

items.text: 3,000+ rules at `github.com/SigmaHQ/sigma`. MITRE ATT&CK tagged. Pull relevant rules, validate FP rate in your environment before production.
store rules in Git with CI/CD pipeline that validates YAML syntax, compiles to SIEM query, and deploys on merge. Version-controlled, reviewable detections.
Test in audit mode → measure FP rate over 2 weeks → add filter conditions for known-good → enable in block/alert → monitor regression monthly.
add `filter_main_legit:` condition blocks to suppress known benign processes. Never suppress by process name alone - use hash + path + parent combination.
online translator for Sigma rules to Splunk/KQL/EQL/QRadar without local sigma-cli install. Good for ad-hoc rule development.

cards.title: YARA Rules
cards.summary: Pattern-based file and memory scanning for malware family detection

items.text: strings section (byte patterns, text, hex sequences) + condition (boolean logic combining string matches with file properties like PE headers, entropy, size).
access import tables, exports, sections, authenticode. `pe.imports("kernel32.dll", "VirtualAlloc")` detects shellcode loaders.
`math.entropy(0, filesize) > 7` catches packed/encrypted payloads. Combine with PE section checks to reduce FPs.
`yara64 -p 4 rule.yar PID` for live process memory. Most EDRs support YARA rules natively for periodic memory scans.
upload rule to VT Intelligence for retroactive corpus scan. Identify related samples for threat actor attribution and infrastructure mapping.
anchor rules with rare, specific byte sequences first. Broad rules (entropy only, single string) are too slow for production scanning at scale.

cards.title: Behavioral Analytics & UEBA
cards.summary: Detect anomalies when signatures won't help - user and entity baseline deviation

items.text: collect 30-90 days of normal behavior before enabling anomaly alerts. Shorter baselines = more noise. Major organizational changes reset baselines.
impossible travel · off-hours privileged access · data staging before exfil · peer group deviations · new admin tool usage.
compare user behavior to their role-based peer group. Developer accessing finance systems is anomalous; IT admin accessing DC is normal.
aggregate risk signals per user/host over a rolling 7-day window. Alert on cumulative score crossing threshold, not individual events.
normal behavior changes (role change, project, seasonal variation). Build supervised feedback loop - analyst feedback retrains models.
Splunk UBA · Microsoft Sentinel UEBA · Securonix · Exabeam · Elastic ML anomaly detection jobs.

cards.title: Network Detection & Response
cards.summary: Network-layer visibility for C2, lateral movement, and data exfiltration detection

items.text: network security monitor generating structured logs: conn.log · http.log · dns.log · ssl.log · kerberos.log · smb.log · weird.log for anomalies.
IDS/IPS with Emerging Threats Open rules. ET Open covers 40,000+ signatures for C2 frameworks, exploit kits, malware callbacks.
TLS client/server fingerprints. Cobalt Strike has a well-known default JA3. Use custom C2 profiles to modify - then detect the profile not the default.
active TLS server fingerprinting. Scan internal hosts to identify C2 team servers by their TLS handshake response characteristics.
automated beaconing detection via Zeek conn.log statistical analysis. Scores connections by beacon probability, connection regularity, and bytes consistency.
long subdomain strings (DGA/exfil), high-entropy labels, unusual query types (TXT for C2), NXDomain storms from DGA malware.

cards.title: ATT&CK Coverage Mapping
cards.summary: Map detection coverage to adversary TTPs - find and fill gaps before attackers exploit them

items.text: visual heatmap of technique coverage. Color-code by: alert (detected), logged (visible, no alert), blind (no visibility). Export as JSON for tracking.
Alert > Logged > Blind. Know your coverage depth per technique, not just binary present/absent.
use CTI to identify which techniques actors targeting your sector use. Cover those techniques first before broad ATT&CK coverage.
tests map 1:1 to ATT&CK. Run atomic test, check SIEM for alert. If no alert → fix detection → document in Navigator.
MITRE D3FEND maps countermeasures to techniques. Use to identify which defensive controls address your coverage gaps.
monthly atomic runs on critical techniques; quarterly full-chain emulations with red team. Document delta in ATT&CK Navigator version control.

cards.title: Detection Rule Development Process
cards.summary: Building high-fidelity, low-noise detections that analysts will trust and act on

items.text: execute technique via Atomic Red Team, observe what data sources fire, build rule from observed real data not documentation assumptions.
broad rules catch more variants but generate FPs that kill analyst trust. Layer multiple narrow rules instead of one broad rule.
understand normal before writing anomaly rules. What does legitimate PsExec use look like in your environment? What cmdlines are normal for certutil?
log every false positive with source system, rule ID, and suppression action taken. Build institutional knowledge base to prevent re-creating known FPs.
rules that never fire in 6 months need review. Either logging gap prevents detection OR the rule is broken. Both need fixing.
rules should be reviewed quarterly. Detection gaps change as attacker TTPs evolve. Old rules for retired techniques consume analyst attention.

title: Technique Detection Matrix
description: Attacker technique mapped to primary detection source and immediate response action. Use this as a first-response reference card.

title: Event ID Reference
description: Critical Windows Security Event IDs and Sysmon events every SOC analyst should know by memory. These form the backbone of Windows detection.

title: Incident Response
description: Structured response from first alert to full recovery. Speed and documentation quality determine outcomes. Contain early, but scope fully before eradicating - premature containment of the wrong host leaves attackers active elsewhere.

rows.label: IR Runbooks
rows.value: Documented procedures per incident type - ransomware · BEC · insider · APT

rows.value: Know crown jewels BEFORE incident - what matters most to the business?

rows.label: Jump bags

rows.label: Tabletops
rows.value: Run scenarios quarterly - muscle memory reduces errors under stress

rows.label: Initial triage
rows.value: True positive confirmation · severity classification · scope estimation

rows.label: Timeline build
rows.value: Patient zero → first malicious action → lateral spread → impact

rows.label: Avoid tunnel vision
rows.value: First compromised host ≠ only compromised host. Assume lateral movement

rows.label: Preserve evidence
rows.value: Capture memory BEFORE rebooting. Preserve logs before rotation window closes

rows.label: Short-term
rows.value: Network isolate via EDR isolation or VLAN ACL change

rows.label: Account containment

rows.label: Silent containment

rows.label: Remove ALL persistence

rows.label: Clean or reimage

rows.value: EVERY credential that could have been exposed MUST be rotated

rows.value: krbtgt TWICE (48hr apart) · all DA accounts · DPAPI backup key

rows.value: Confirm clean state before returning to production

rows.label: Enhanced monitoring
rows.value: Monitor closely post-recovery - secondary persistence is common

rows.label: Root cause analysis
rows.value: Which control failed? Why? What prevents recurrence?

rows.label: Detection updates
rows.value: Every IR generates at least one new detection rule - enforce this norm

cards.title: Memory Forensics
cards.summary: Capture and analyze volatile memory - injected code, C2 connections, in-memory credentials

items.text: `winpmem` (Windows free) · `LiME` (Linux kernel module) · `osxpmem` (macOS). Always hash the dump immediately after capture.
`pstree` · `netscan` · `cmdline` · `malfind` (injected code) · `dlllist` · `handles`
identifies memory regions with MZ headers + executable + no backing file + RWX permissions. Primary tool for finding injected shellcode and reflective DLL loads.
`pypykatz` on memory dump extracts LSASS credentials. Use to determine credential scope in active incidents without rebooting host.
mount memory image as a filesystem. Browse process memory as files/directories. Search strings across all processes simultaneously.
capture memory BEFORE rebooting or isolating. Network isolation is fine. Reboot destroys all volatile evidence including C2 in-memory implants.

cards.title: Disk & Artifact Forensics
cards.summary: Persistent artifacts remain even after malware deletion - the forensic record is deep on Windows

items.text: Master File Table contains timestamps for every file operation. Find deleted malware by MFT entry even if file is deleted from directory listing.
`C:\Windows\Prefetch\` records execution with timestamps and loaded files. Confirms if a binary ran even if it was deleted post-execution.
registry record of every EXE that touched the filesystem. Persists across reboots. Find malware execution history even without process logs.
`C:\Windows\appcompat\Programs\Amcache.hve` stores SHA1 hashes of recently executed binaries. Enables hash-based threat hunting on historical execution.
`EvtxECmd` + `Timeline Explorer` · `PECmd` (Prefetch) · `AmcacheParser` · `ShimCacheParser`. Free and industry-standard.
recent file access history. Reveals what files the attacker opened, staged, or exfiltrated. Survives file deletion.

cards.title: Active Directory IR
cards.summary: AD-wide compromise response - credential reset order, golden ticket invalidation, trust audit

items.text: collect current AD snapshot, run BloodHound CE. Map all paths reachable from compromised accounts before resetting anything.
MUST rotate TWICE with ≥10 hours between rotations. Single rotation does not invalidate all outstanding golden tickets. Coordinate timing with all sites.
Domain Admins → Enterprise Admins → built-in Administrator → service accounts in that priority order. Reset before notifying end users to prevent reuse.
if attacker had DCSync rights, they have the DPAPI backup key. All user DPAPI secrets (browser passwords, credential manager) are compromised and decryptable.
review all domain trusts for recently added or modified trusts. Attackers add trusts for persistent access that survives password resets.
run `PingCastle` after AD remediation for quick security posture score and remaining risk identification.

cards.title: Cloud IR - Entra ID & M365
cards.summary: Responding to cloud identity compromise - token revocation, app audit, CAP hardening

items.text: `Revoke-MgUserSignInSession` via Microsoft Graph. Kills all active tokens including refresh tokens. Password reset alone does NOT revoke tokens in Entra ID.
check all app registrations and consent grants since compromise window. Attackers register backdoor apps with mail.read permissions that survive password resets.
delegated permissions survive credential resets. Audit and remove all attacker-granted consent grants via `Get-MgOauth2PermissionGrant`.
review Exchange Online, SharePoint, OneDrive, Teams, Azure AD operations during the compromise window. Map all data accessed.
attacker may have registered their own FIDO2 key or MFA app. Audit all authentication methods per user since compromise date.
every Conditional Access exclusion is a potential bypass path. Map the specific CAP gap the attacker exploited and close it.

cards.title: Ransomware Response
cards.summary: Ransomware IR is distinct - speed, backup integrity, and legal considerations are paramount

items.text: network segment (not full shutdown). Preserve forensic evidence while preventing further spread. Full shutdown destroys evidence and may worsen encryption.
`ID Ransomware` at nomoreransom.org. Some variants have free decryptors. Identifying strain also confirms if pre-encryption exfil occurred (double extortion).
test backup integrity IMMEDIATELY. Ransomware groups target backup infrastructure first (Veeam exploitation is common). Contaminated backups = prolonged recovery.
look 2-6 weeks back for data staging, large transfers, credential harvesting. Double extortion = backup restore doesn't prevent leak publication.

items.lead: Do NOT pay without legal review
items.text: OFAC sanctions apply to some ransomware groups. Payment may be illegal. Notify cyber insurer immediately - policies have strict notification windows.
usually phishing or exposed/unpatched RDP. Trace initial access completely. Rebuilt systems return to same environment and re-compromise without root cause fix.

cards.title: Evidence & Chain of Custody
cards.summary: Forensic evidence handling for legal proceedings and root cause accuracy

items.text: volatile evidence priority: running processes → network connections → memory dump → disk image. Document acquisition timestamps.
SHA256 hash of every collected artifact immediately after collection. Record in chain of custody documentation. Any hash mismatch invalidates evidence.
use hardware write blockers for disk acquisition. Software write blockers acceptable if hardware unavailable. Never mount a disk without write protection.
who collected, when, from where (hostname, serial, IP), acquisition method, tool version, hash values, custodian chain.
export logs to immutable storage before rotation. Many orgs lose critical evidence to log rotation during IR when investigation timeline extends.
`FTK Imager` (free, disk acquisition) · `Autopsy` (open-source analysis) · `Magnet AXIOM` (commercial, full DFIR platform).

title: Threat Hunting
description: Proactive hunting for adversaries that evaded automated detection. Hypothesis-driven, intelligence-informed, and data-validated. Every hunt either finds something or produces a new detection rule.

callouts.title: Hunt Outcome Rule
callouts.body: Every threat hunt must produce one of two outcomes: a finding that requires response or a new detection rule that covers the hunted pattern going forward. A hunt that produces neither was a waste of analyst time.

queries.title: Find processes spawning from suspicious parents
queries.code:
index=sysmon EventCode=1
| eval suspicious_parent=if(match(ParentImage,"(?i)(winword|excel|powerpnt|outlook|mshta|wscript|cscript)"), 1, 0)
| where suspicious_parent=1 AND NOT (Image LIKE "%splunk%" OR Image LIKE "%sysmon%")
| table _time Computer User ParentImage Image CommandLine

queries.title: LSASS access attempts (non-AV)
queries.code:
index=sysmon EventCode=10 TargetImage="*lsass.exe"
| where GrantedAccess IN ("0x1FFFFF", "0x1010", "0x0410", "0x1438")
| where NOT SourceImage IN ("*CrowdStrike*", "*MsMpEng*", "*Sysmon64*")
| table _time Computer SourceImage GrantedAccess CallTrace

queries.title: Kerberoasting - RC4 service tickets
queries.code:
index=winevent EventCode=4769
| where TicketEncryptionType="0x17" AND ServiceName!="krbtgt"
| where ServiceName!="$" AND NOT ServiceName LIKE "%$"
| stats count by Account_Name ServiceName Client_Address
| where count > 3

queries.title: Network connections from unusual processes
queries.code:
index=sysmon EventCode=3
| where match(Image,"(?i)(mshta|wscript|cscript|regsvr32|certutil|bitsadmin)")
| where Initiated="true" AND DestinationPort IN (80,443,8080,8443)
| where NOT DestinationIp LIKE "10.*" AND NOT DestinationIp LIKE "192.168.*"
| table _time Computer Image DestinationIp DestinationPort

queries.title: New WMI subscriptions (attacker persistence)
queries.code:
index=wmi EventCode=5861
| search NOT Consumer LIKE "*Microsoft*" NOT Consumer LIKE "*SCM*"
| table _time ComputerName Consumer Filter Query

cards.title: Hunt Methodology
cards.summary: Structured approach - intelligence-driven, hypothesis-based, data-validated

items.text: what TTPs are actors targeting your sector using? CTI reports · ISAC alerts · recent IR findings · CISA advisories · vendor threat reports.
"If APT29 is present, we expect OAuth token theft patterns in sign-in logs with impossible travel." Specific, testable, falsifiable.
do we have the log sources to test this hypothesis? If not, the hunt reveals a visibility gap that must be fixed.
run queries, analyze results, document every pivot. Unexplained anomalies warrant investigation even if not the original hypothesis target.
finding (escalate to IR) or new detection rule (codify the hunting query as an automated alert for ongoing coverage).
weekly structured hunts aligned to threat intel. Ad-hoc after major CVE disclosure, industry breach report, or new attacker technique publication.

cards.title: Hunt: C2 Beaconing
cards.summary: Detect regular callback patterns that signature-based rules miss entirely

items.text: connections to same destination at regular intervals. Even with jitter, statistical patterns persist across 50+ samples. Low deviation = automated callback.
processes Zeek conn.log, scores each src/dst pair by beacon probability. Prioritizes by connection count, byte consistency, and interval regularity.
`| eventstats count avg(bytes) as ab by src dest | where count>20 AND ab<2000 AND ab>50` - small, consistent, frequent = C2 pattern.
HTTP/S connections over 60 seconds with low byte count. Interactive C2 keeps connections alive with minimal data transfer between operator actions.
Cobalt Strike default JA3 is `07d14d16d21d21d07c42d41d00041d24a458a375eef0c576d23a7bab9a9fb1`. Custom C2 profiles change this - hunt for internal JA3 patterns against known-bad databases.
regular low-TTL queries to same domain or parent domain. DGA beaconing creates NXDomain storms. Both are detectable via Zeek dns.log analysis.

cards.title: Hunt: Living Off the Land
cards.summary: Find attacker abuse of legitimate Windows tools - LOLBins that evade AV/EDR signatures

items.text: understand which LOLBins are legitimately used in your environment. certutil for certificate management is normal; certutil downloading URLs is not.
encoded commands (`-enc`) · download cradles (Net.WebClient, IWR) · bypass execution policy flags · `-WindowStyle Hidden` combinations.
any network connection from certutil.exe is high-confidence IOC. No legitimate use case requires certutil to make outbound HTTP connections.
Office/PDF reader → PowerShell · Explorer → cmd → PowerShell · mshta.exe → any child · wscript.exe spawning network tools.
creates WmiPrvSE.exe child processes on target. Hunt WmiPrvSE children that aren't normal administrative tools in your environment.
spawning network connections or executing .NET assemblies from user-writable paths. Both are signed Microsoft binaries that AV typically trusts.

cards.title: Hunt: Persistence Mechanisms
cards.summary: Find attacker-installed persistence that survived initial containment actions

items.text: collect `AutorunsToWinEventLog` output fleet-wide. Diff against known-good baseline collected before incident. Any new entry is suspicious.
new tasks with encoded PowerShell in actions, tasks created by unusual authors, tasks with binary paths in user-writable directories.
`Get-WMIObject __FilterToConsumerBinding`. Any event subscription not in your known-good baseline is attacker persistence. WMI persistence survives reimages if AD objects persist.
HKCU CLSIDs that shadow HKLM entries. `HKCU\Software\Classes\CLSID\` InprocServer32 entries pointing to user-writable paths = DLL persistence.
Process Monitor "NAME NOT FOUND" DLL searches in user-writable directories from legitimate signed binaries. Classic persistence technique bypassing AppLocker.
`sc qc` on all new services. Services with binary paths in AppData, Temp, or other user-writable directories are almost always malicious.

title: SOAR Playbooks
description: Automate enrichment and low-stakes response actions freely. Gate destructive actions (block, disable, isolate) behind analyst approval. Human judgment in the loop for all consequential decisions.

callouts.title: Automation Principle
callouts.body: Automate what is repeatable and low-risk: enrichment, notification, ticket creation, log retrieval. Require human approval for: account disable, host isolation, firewall block, email deletion. The goal is speed + accuracy, not removing human judgment from consequential actions.

cards.title: Phishing Triage Playbook
cards.summary: Automated phishing response from report to resolution

items.text: user submits suspicious email via "Report Phishing" button OR email gateway alert fires on incoming message.
extract all IOCs: sender, reply-to, sending IP, URLs, attachment hashes. Submit to VirusTotal, URLScan, and internal TIP simultaneously.
query SIEM for all users who received messages from same sender in last 30 days. Query EDR for any execution of attachment hashes fleet-wide.
if any IOC is known-malicious AND no execution found: auto-block sender + URLs + quarantine similar messages. Create P2 ticket with enriched context.
if execution of attachment is found on any endpoint: pause automation, page on-call analyst, create P1 incident with all enrichment pre-populated.
bulk-purge matching emails from all mailboxes via Graph API `Purge-AIPContent`. Notify affected users with guidance.

cards.title: Compromised Account Playbook
cards.summary: Identity incident response from detection to full remediation

items.text: impossible travel alert · Entra ID Protection high-risk sign-in · multiple MFA push rejections · anomalous Graph API activity.
enrich: pull user's manager, department, recent logins (last 30 days), MFA methods registered, app consent grants, recent email forwarding rules.
query SIEM for all activity from this account + all IPs used in last 24 hours. Check if IPs appear in threat intel feeds.
analyst reviews enriched context. If confirmed compromise: approve account disable + token revocation.
disable account in AD/Entra · revoke all tokens via `Revoke-MgUserSignInSession` · remove forwarding rules · notify manager and IT.
hunt for lateral movement: query all hosts where account authenticated in last 7 days. Check for persistence mechanisms on each host via Velociraptor.

cards.title: IOC Block Playbook
cards.summary: Automated IOC blocking across all defense layers simultaneously

items.text: analyst submits IOC · CTI feed pushes high-confidence indicator · IR team generates IOCs from active incident.
validate IOC format and type (hash/IP/domain/URL). Check against internal whitelist. Query VirusTotal and internal TIP for confidence score.
hunt for IOC presence in environment: SIEM historical query (30 days) + EDR fleet hunt + proxy logs + DNS logs. Report any matches immediately.

items.lead: If IOC confidence > 80% AND no internal hits
items.text: auto-block across: DNS sinkhole · proxy URL block · EDR custom IOC · firewall block (IP) · email gateway sender block.
escalate immediately. Do not block until analyst reviews potential attacker notification risk. Create P1 with affected asset list.
add IOC to threat intel platform with context. Set expiry date (IPs: 90 days · domains: 180 days · hashes: permanent). Create JIRA task for periodic review.

cards.title: Critical Alert Enrichment Playbook
cards.summary: Auto-enrich every P1/P2 alert before it reaches an analyst's queue

items.text: any P1 or P2 alert from SIEM, EDR, identity, or email platforms.
CMDB lookup: asset owner · criticality tier · last patch date · business unit. EDR status: protection enabled · last seen · agent version.
HR system: role · department · manager · employment status. AD: group memberships · last password reset · MFA status · recent logins.
submit all IOCs to VT/Shodan/PassiveDNS. Query internal TIP for prior sightings. Check CISA KEV for CVEs if vuln-related.
query case management for prior incidents involving same user/host/IP in last 90 days. Link related cases.
create enriched ticket with all context pre-populated. Assign to correct queue based on alert type. Notify asset owner if P1.

title: Identity & Access Security
description: Identity is the new perimeter. Credential compromise bypasses all network controls. Hardening identity systems is the highest-ROI defensive investment for most organizations today.

callouts.title: MFA is not equal
callouts.body: TOTP/push MFA is bypassable via AitM proxy (EvilGinx, Modlishka). It provides protection against password spray and credential stuffing but NOT against targeted phishing. For privileged accounts, only FIDO2/passkeys provide phishing-resistant MFA. Enforcing TOTP on Domain Admins and calling it "secure" is a false sense of security.

cards.title: MFA Strength Hierarchy
cards.summary: Not all MFA is equal - choose the right tier for each use case

items.text: hardware key (YubiKey) or device-bound passkey. Cryptographically bound to domain. Defeats AitM/EvilGinx completely. Required for all Tier 0 accounts.
items.note: Windows Hello for Business provides device-bound phishing-resistant credentials on Windows endpoints.

items.text: smart card or virtual smart card. Phishing-resistant, device-bound, no shared secret.

items.lead: Authenticator app push / TOTP ⚠️ AitM bypassable
items.text: easily bypassed by reverse proxy. Better than nothing but insufficient for privileged access. Enable number matching + IP context to reduce fatigue attacks.
SIM swap, SS7 attacks, social engineering. Use only as absolute last resort fallback with compensating controls.
attackers spam push notifications until the user accidentally accepts. Enable number matching and require additional context to defeat this.
Tier 0 accounts with FIDO2 first → all admins → all users via Conditional Access → MFA registration campaign for remaining users.

cards.title: Privileged Access Management
cards.summary: Protect, monitor, and govern privileged accounts - the keys to the entire kingdom

items.text: Tier 0 (DC/CA/PKI/backup), Tier 1 (servers), Tier 2 (workstations). Strict credential isolation - no Tier 0 admin account used on Tier 2 systems.
dedicated hardened devices for admin tasks. No email, no web browsing, no untrusted software. Connected to management network only.
PIM / Azure Privileged Identity Management. Elevate only when needed. Time-boxed (4-8hr max). Requires justification + approval + MFA.
PowerShell constrained runspaces limiting admin to specific cmdlets needed for their role. No interactive shell - no PowerShell.exe access.
CyberArk · BeyondTrust · Delinea. Auto-rotate privileged passwords. Session recording for all privileged sessions. Dual control for most critical accounts.
unique local admin password per machine. Stops lateral movement via shared local admin credentials (common initial spread vector).

cards.title: Active Directory Hardening
cards.summary: Reduce the AD attack surface - the primary target in the majority of enterprise breaches

items.text: block NTLM where possible, enforce Kerberos. NTLM cannot be MFA-protected and enables PtH attacks. Monitor for RC4 ticket requests (should be AES-only).
audit and eliminate where possible. Unconstrained delegation on non-DC systems amplifies golden ticket and credential relay attacks significantly.
audit accounts with AdminCount=1. Any unexpected account with AdminCount=1 may have inherited protected group membership through AD's AdminSDHolder propagation.
ensure ALL accounts have pre-auth required. Accounts with pre-auth disabled are AS-REP roastable - attackers can request encrypted tickets offline for cracking.
run `Locksmith` to identify ESC1-ESC8 vulnerabilities. ESC1 (SAN in request) is the most exploited. Fix before attackers find it.
disable unused accounts immediately. Stale service accounts with SPNs are Kerberoasting targets. Enforce password policies and review weekly.

cards.title: Conditional Access Policies
cards.summary: Zero trust access control - enforce context for every authentication decision

items.text: require MFA for all users · block all legacy auth protocols (IMAP/POP3/SMTP AUTH/Basic) · require compliant device for sensitive apps.
Entra ID Protection risk signals: block high-risk sign-ins · require step-up auth for medium-risk · log low-risk for investigation.
enforce FIDO2/WHfB for all admin roles, VPN access, and sensitive applications. Use Authentication Strength policies for fine-grained control.
require Intune-managed and compliant device for access to M365, cloud storage, and sensitive internal applications.
every CAP exclusion is a potential bypass. Review all exclusions quarterly. Break-glass accounts should be the ONLY permanent exclusion with monitoring.
always test new CAPs in report-only mode for 2-4 weeks. Measure sign-in impact before enforcing. Blocking users produces IT tickets that undermine security programs.

title: System Hardening
description: Reduce attack surface through configuration management and defense-in-depth controls. Every unnecessary feature is potential attack surface - the principle of least functionality.

cards.title: Windows Endpoint Hardening
cards.summary: CIS benchmark, ASR rules, and LOLBin restriction for workstations

items.text: enable all 16 ASR rules in audit mode first, then transition to block after 2-4 weeks. Highest-value: block Office spawning processes · block macro downloads · block credential theft from LSASS.
hypervisor-protected LSASS prevents Pass-the-Hash and DPAPI key extraction even with LSASS handle access. Enable on all Windows 10/11 endpoints via Group Policy.
kernel-mode code integrity. Only allow signed code. Kills BYOVD attacks at the kernel driver level. More effective than AppLocker but more complex to deploy.
blocks Add-Type, New-Object, reflection, and other post-exploitation PS capabilities. Enforced via AppLocker or WDAC policy.
captures all PowerShell script content, even when scripts are loaded from memory or base64-decoded at runtime. Crucial for PS-based attacker detection.
block execution from user-writable paths: AppData · Temp · Downloads · user profile. Stops majority of commodity malware that writes to user paths.
block all VBA macros or restrict to code-signed only via Group Policy Trust Center settings. Document any legitimate macro use and provide alternative workflows.

cards.title: ADCS Hardening
cards.summary: Active Directory Certificate Services - most dangerous misconfiguration area in enterprise AD

items.text: run `Locksmith` against your ADCS environment. Automatically identifies ESC1-ESC8 vulnerabilities with remediation guidance. Run quarterly.
remove `ENROLLEE_SUPPLIES_SUBJECT` flag from all non-CA certificate templates. This flag allows requesters to specify any SAN including domain admin UPNs.
remove Write permissions on certificate templates for non-admin users. Template write access allows modification of template properties to add ESC1-style vulnerabilities.
remove EDITF_ATTRIBUTESUBJECTALTNAME2 flag from CA configuration. This flag allows SAN specification on any template, not just those configured for it.
enable all CA audit events: 4886 cert issued · 4887 cert with SAN · 4899 template modified. None of these are enabled by default. Must be explicitly configured per CA.
CA servers are Tier 0 assets equal to Domain Controllers. Apply same access controls, monitoring, and physical security as DCs.
alert on certificates issued with SANs containing privileged UPNs · off-hours certificate issuance · unusual templates · certificates with excessive validity periods.

cards.title: Patch Management
cards.summary: Risk-prioritized vulnerability remediation - focus on what attackers are actually exploiting

items.text: Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog at cisa.gov/kev. Treat as P0. Patch within 2 weeks regardless of CVSS score or internal risk tolerance policy. These are being actively exploited now.
Exploit Prediction Scoring System scores by probability of exploitation within 30 days. Better real-world risk signal than CVSS severity score alone.
a CVSS 7.0 on an internet-facing system is higher priority than CVSS 9.8 on an isolated internal host. Exposure context matters more than severity score.
pre-approved process for critical CVEs. Cannot wait for monthly maintenance windows when a CVSS 9.8 with active exploitation is published.
Critical+internet-facing: 7 days · Critical+internal: 30 days · High: 60 days · Medium: 90 days. Track SLA compliance rates as a security metric.
browsers, PDF readers, Office, VPN clients are more frequently targeted than the OS. Automate these via Intune/SCCM software deployment policies.

cards.title: Backup & Recovery Hardening
cards.summary: Ransomware-resistant backup strategy - the last line of defense when all else fails

items.text: 3 copies · 2 different media · 1 offsite · 1 immutable/offline · 0 errors confirmed by restore testing. All five criteria must be met continuously.
S3 Object Lock / Azure Blob immutable storage. Ransomware cannot delete or encrypt immutable copies even with storage admin credentials.
air-gapped tapes or offline disks physically disconnected from the network. Cannot be reached by ransomware spreading through network credentials.
backup service accounts in dedicated OU with no regular network access. Attackers specifically target Veeam, Commvault, and backup agents to destroy recovery capability.
quarterly restore tests across different systems. Test full server restore, not just file recovery. Most orgs discover backup failures during incidents when it's too late.
document and test Recovery Time Objective and Recovery Point Objective per system tier. Executives need realistic timelines during incidents, not estimates.

title: Network Security Controls
description: Every lateral movement the attacker makes should cross a monitoring point. Segmentation, DNS control, and encrypted traffic inspection are the key network defensive investments.

cards.title: Network Segmentation
cards.summary: Limit blast radius through logical and physical network separation

items.text: User · Server · Management · Guest · IoT · OT each in dedicated VLANs. Firewall rules between segments - not router-only ACLs.
DCs · CA servers · backup infrastructure in separate management VLAN. Access only via jump hosts. No workstation-to-DC direct connectivity except domain traffic.
block TCP 445 (SMB) between workstations. This single rule prevents PsExec lateral movement across the majority of the flat enterprise network.
host-based firewall policies allowing only required application flows. Stops east-west movement even within same VLAN when attackers gain workstation access.
outbound connections should be explicitly allowed, not default-permit. Block direct-to-internet from servers. Force all traffic through proxy for inspection.
application-layer access control. Verify user + device + context before each connection. Never trust, always verify approach for internal resources.

cards.title: DNS Security
cards.summary: DNS is used in nearly every attack - logging, filtering, and sinkholing are essential controls

items.text: log all DNS queries with requesting process (Sysmon Event 22 on endpoints, DNS server query logging internally). Without process-to-query correlation, C2-over-DNS is nearly invisible.
redirect malicious domains to internal sinkhole IP via RPZ. Log and alert on all connections. Identifies infections missed by other controls.
Cisco Umbrella · Cloudflare Gateway · Quad9. Filter malicious domains at resolver level. Adds threat intelligence-based blocking without endpoint agent.
block or proxy DNS-over-HTTPS. Attackers use DoH (Cloudflare/Google DoH) to bypass traditional DNS monitoring and filtering. Block port 853 and well-known DoH endpoints.
high-entropy domain names, NXDomain storms, unusual query types (TXT/MX for C2). Detect malware with domain generation algorithm via statistical analysis of query patterns.
DNS queries with subdomains over 50 characters are likely DNS tunneling or DGA exfiltration. Alert on this pattern with low FP rate.

cards.title: Email Security Hardening
cards.summary: Technical controls to reduce phishing delivery and BEC success rates

items.text: publish strict SPF: `v=spf1 include:... -all` (hard fail). Reject unauthorized senders. Monitor DMARC reports to identify spoofing attempts.
cryptographically sign all outbound email. Validates sender authenticity and prevents header tampering in transit. Use 2048-bit RSA or Ed25519 keys.
`v=DMARC1; p=reject; rua=mailto:dmarc@domain.com`. Enforce rejection and receive aggregate reports. Start with p=none to see traffic before enforcing.
detonate attachments before delivery. Catches macro-less payloads, LNK files, ISO/IMG files that AV misses on static analysis. Zero-hour detonation coverage.
rescan URLs when user actually clicks, not just at delivery. Catches URLs that were clean at delivery but weaponized afterward (common AitM phishing technique).
block external emails impersonating internal domains and lookalike domains. BEC relies on this vector. DMARC + anti-spoofing in MDO/Proofpoint blocks the majority.

cards.title: Web Proxy & TLS Inspection
cards.summary: Inspect encrypted traffic and control egress - required to detect modern attacks

items.text: decrypt HTTPS traffic for malware scanning, DLP, and C2 detection. Without TLS inspection, approximately 80% of C2 traffic is invisible to proxy and IDS/IPS.
block uncategorized + newly-registered + parked domains. Attackers use freshly-registered domains for C2. Newly-registered domain block catches infrastructure before it appears in threat feeds.
alert or block `curl` · `python-requests` · `Invoke-WebRequest` user-agents from non-developer systems. Automated tool usage is a strong signal.
detect known C2 frameworks by TLS client hello fingerprint at the proxy layer. Cobalt Strike's default JA3 is detectable even on port 443.
force all endpoint TCP 80/443 through the proxy. Block direct internet egress from endpoints. Without this, C2 channels bypass all proxy-based detection.
alert on connections to domains registered less than 30 days ago. Freshly-registered domains are a strong signal for C2 and phishing infrastructure.

title: Cloud Defense Operations
description: Azure/Entra ID, AWS, and GCP defensive controls. Cloud-native detection, identity security, and infrastructure hardening for environments where traditional network controls don't apply.

cards.title: Microsoft 365 / Entra ID Defense
cards.summary: Detect and respond to cloud identity attacks in Microsoft environments

items.text: risk-based sign-in policies. Block high-risk. Require step-up for medium-risk. Risk detections: atypical travel · anonymous IP · malware-linked IP · leaked credentials.
enable for all workloads: Exchange · SharePoint · Teams · Azure AD. 90-day retention on E3, 1 year on E5. Must be explicitly enabled - not on by default for all orgs.
block IMAP, POP3, SMTP AUTH, Basic Auth, EWS without modern auth via Conditional Access. Legacy auth bypasses MFA entirely - major attack vector for credential stuffing.
alert on new OAuth app consent grants for sensitive permissions (mail.read, files.readwrite, mail.send). Attacker registers backdoor app through consent phishing.
enable `MicrosoftGraphActivityLogs` in Diagnostic Settings. Not enabled by default. Essential for post-compromise investigation of token theft and data access.
SaaS visibility, DLP, and anomaly detection across M365 and third-party apps. OAuth app governance and risky app blocking.

cards.title: AWS Defense
cards.summary: CloudTrail, GuardDuty, Security Hub - detecting and responding to AWS attacks

items.text: enable organization-wide, multi-region trail to S3 with CloudTrail Insights and log file integrity validation. Foundation of all AWS logging. Disable of CloudTrail = immediate P1 alert.
enable in every region including regions you don't use. Threat detection for IAM anomalies, network threats, S3 threats. Cost: ~$3/1M events. Enable S3 and EKS protection too.
aggregate GuardDuty + Macie + Inspector + Config findings into centralized view. Run CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark assessment continuously.
organization-level guardrails. Deny dangerous actions org-wide: prevent IAM user creation · prevent CloudTrail disable · prevent public S3 bucket creation · restrict regions.
detects overly permissive policies and external access to resources. Run continuously. Alert on any resource with external access not on approved list.
anomaly detection on API call rate and error rate. Detects credential abuse (unusual call volume) and scanning activity (unusual error rate) automatically.

cards.title: Cloud Posture Management
cards.summary: Continuously assess cloud configuration against benchmarks and detect configuration drift

items.text: multi-cloud posture management. CIS benchmark scoring for Azure/AWS/GCP. Attack path analysis shows exploitable chained misconfigurations. Prioritize by attack path risk, not individual finding.
open-source multi-cloud assessment. AWS/Azure/GCP. 300+ checks with CIS/PCI/HIPAA/NIST mappings. Run weekly and feed findings to SIEM for trending.
attacker's perspective of your cloud environment. Find exploitable IAM paths, exposed services, and secrets before attackers do. Great for red team exercises and pre-engagement reconnaissance.
IaC security scanning for Terraform, CloudFormation, Kubernetes manifests. Shift-left cloud security - catch misconfigurations before deployment in CI/CD pipeline.
public S3 buckets · overpermissioned IAM roles (wildcard actions) · missing MFA for root/console · unencrypted databases · unrestricted security groups (0.0.0.0/0).
AWS Config or Azure Policy enforce compliance continuously. Automated remediation for clear violations (e.g., auto-encrypt unencrypted EBS volumes on creation).

cards.title: Kubernetes Security
cards.summary: Container and orchestration security - RBAC, network policies, runtime protection

items.text: least privilege roles. No `cluster-admin` bindings for application workloads. Audit all ClusterRoleBindings quarterly. Wildcard resource/verb permissions are a critical finding.
default-deny ingress and egress, whitelist required pod-to-pod connections. Prevents lateral movement between pods even within the same namespace.
open-source runtime security using syscall-based detection. Rules for container breakout, privilege escalation, shell execution in containers, and sensitive file access.
enforce `restricted` policy for all namespaces. Blocks privileged containers, hostPath mounts, hostNetwork, and other escalation primitives.
External Secrets Operator + HashiCorp Vault or AWS Secrets Manager. Never store secrets in ConfigMaps or environment variables in plain text.
Trivy/Grype in pipeline. Block images with critical CVEs before deployment. Sign images with Cosign and enforce signature verification at admission.

title: Threat Intelligence
description: Intelligence drives hunting prioritization, detection coverage, and hardening focus. The goal is operationalization - transforming CTI reports into actionable detections and controls, not building an intelligence collection program.

cards.title: TI Platforms
cards.summary: Aggregate, correlate, and operationalize threat intelligence

items.text: open-source TIP with STIX/TAXII. Share and consume IOCs. Community-driven. Self-hosted.
structured threat actor, campaign, and TTP tracking with ATT&CK integration.
dark web, paste site, technical data. Real-time risk scoring per IP/domain/hash.
sector-specific sharing with peers seeing the same threats targeting your industry.
free, high-quality. AA advisories provide nation-state TTPs with detection guidance.

cards.title: Malware Analysis
cards.summary: Understand threats through sample analysis - extract IOCs, TTPs, and signatures

items.text: extracts capabilities from PE files, mapped to ATT&CK. Instant TTP analysis without RE skills.
online detonation with full behavior report, network IOCs, process tree.
self-hosted. Privacy-sensitive samples. Configuration extraction for malware families.
deep binary analysis. C2 decryption routines, config extraction, variant identification.
Mandiant's tool. Extract obfuscated strings from binaries that regular strings command misses.

cards.title: Dark Web Monitoring
cards.summary: Monitor for credential leaks, data dumps, and attacker targeting

items.text: free domain monitoring. Alert on credential exposure in breach databases.
infostealer log monitoring. Catches credentials stolen by Redline/Raccoon/Vidar that never appear in public breach databases.
dark web forum posts, marketplace listings, actor communications involving your brand or data.
newly registered lookalike domains, typosquatted names. Phishing infrastructure discovery before use.
`trufflehog` · `gitleaks`. Scan public repos for accidentally committed API keys and credentials.

title: Deception Technology
description: Honeypots, canary tokens, and deceptive credentials give near-zero false positive alerts - any interaction is malicious by definition. The highest signal-to-noise ratio in the defensive toolkit.

callouts.title: Deception Value Proposition
callouts.body: Canary tokens and honeypots are the only detection class with near-zero false positive rate. No legitimate user accesses a fake admin password document, uses a fake AWS key, or connects to a honeypot server. Any alert from deception technology is a confirmed attacker action and should immediately trigger P1 response.

cards.title: Canary Tokens
cards.summary: Tripwires embedded in documents, credentials, and files - instant alert on access

items.text: free at `canarytokens.org`. Token types: Word/Excel docs · PDFs · web bugs · AWS access keys · DNS tokens · email addresses · Windows folder breadcrumbs.
embed in documents named "passwords," "network_diagram," "IT_Admin_Creds." Token fires when opened, revealing opener IP/hostname. Near-zero legitimate access.
place in source code, S3 config files, developer documentation. Any AWS API call attempt fires immediate alert regardless of credential validity.
fake internal hostnames (PROD-DC-02-MGMT) in internal documentation. Any DNS lookup reveals attacker has read internal docs and is mapping infrastructure.
fake privileged-looking accounts with canary passwords. Login attempt from any source = confirmed attacker conducting internal recon.
"Company_Passwords_2024.xlsx" and "Network_Topology.pdf" on shared drives. Opened = attacker actively browsing file shares for credential material.

cards.title: Honeypots & AD Deception
cards.summary: Fake systems and AD objects that attract and detect internal reconnaissance

items.text: commercial hardware/virtual honeypots. Emulates Windows servers, Linux hosts, Cisco devices, and more. Alert fires on any connection attempt. No false positives.
free open-source. Simulates SSH, HTTP, FTP, SNMP, SMB, and Telnet services. Deploy as hidden internal hosts on each VLAN for lateral movement detection.
fake privileged accounts (svc_backup, IT_Admin, SQLSvcAcct) with real-looking SPNs. Kerberoast attempt or auth attempt reveals active enumeration.
service principal names on honey accounts. Any Kerberoasting attempt against them triggers detection without any false positive risk.
fake DC or server computer objects in AD. RPC/SMB connection attempts reveal an attacker has enumerated AD and is attempting lateral movement to these objects.
scatter across all VLANs. Use realistic naming conventions matching your environment. There is no legitimate reason for any internal system to connect to a honeypot host.

title: Vulnerability Management
description: Risk-prioritized vulnerability identification and remediation. CVSS scores alone are insufficient - contextualize with exposure, exploitability, and asset criticality to focus remediation resources.

cards.title: Scanning & Prioritization
cards.summary: Credentialed scanning and risk-based prioritization

items.text: industry standard. Always use credentialed scans - unauthenticated misses 80% of findings.
template-based scanner with massive community template library for specific CVE detection.
Known Exploited Vulnerabilities are P0 regardless of CVSS score.
exploitation probability score. Better risk signal than CVSS alone for prioritization decisions.
weekly credentialed internal · daily internet-facing · continuous for cloud assets.

cards.title: Attack Surface Management
cards.summary: Discover and monitor all internet-facing assets continuously

items.text: Censys/Shodan EASM platforms. Discover all assets exposed to the internet, including shadow IT and forgotten subdomains.
`crt.sh` / `certstream`. Monitor CT logs for new certs issued to your domains. Catches phishing and subdomain takeover risks.
alert on new subdomains especially on cloud providers (S3, Azure Blob, GitHub Pages). Subdomain takeover is a common initial access vector.
alerts when new services appear on your IP ranges. Catches exposed RDP, SSH, databases before attackers find them.
many internet-facing assets are unknown to security. Cloud accounts, dev test environments, forgotten applications.

cards.title: Remediation SLAs
cards.summary: Risk-tiered patching timelines that organizations can actually meet

items.text: P0 CISA KEV - 7 days. No exceptions. Pre-approved emergency change process required to meet this SLA.
Critical + Internet - 14 days. High business risk. Escalate to CISO if SLA cannot be met.
Critical Internal - 30 days. Standard change process acceptable.
High + Internet - 30 days. Include in next patching cycle.
High Internal - 60 days. Track in VM platform for SLA compliance.
Medium - 90 days. Batched with regular maintenance. Reprioritize if EPSS increases.

title: Blue Team Tool Arsenal
description: Essential defensive tools by function. The best tools are the ones your team uses consistently - invest in training and process, not just purchasing licenses.
